interpretation_history.interpretation: Of the 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) carry an ACTUAL read type and 1240 (41%) carry an ESTIMATED read type — disputes are not predominantly tied to estimated/substituted reads, so the surge cannot be explained mainly by missing/estimated reads alone.

The CRM record shows that despite the ticket volume surge, tickets are currently being answered within the service SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days vs a 3.0-day target), indicating response-handling throughput is not currently degraded even as volume doubled.

The route-log record shows manual read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 at 88% against a 95% target across 9200 manual read accounts, a 7-point shortfall in field meter read collection during the exact dispute-surge period.

Monthly CRM dispute counts (610, 590, 1180, 1260 for Jun-Sep 2026) confirm a real volume surge: baseline of ~590-610/month roughly doubled to ~1180-1260/month starting in August and persisting into September. This validates the magnitude and August onset of the surge but says nothing about its cause.
